gloss: after all; you see; the thing is

definitions.gloss: after all; you see; the thing is
definitions.explanation: Introduces a key explanatory fact or reason that makes the speaker's point understandable. A more casual, conversational variant of なにしろ.

examples.japanese: なにせ{初|はじ}めてだから{緊張|きんちょう}するよ。
examples.english: The thing is, it's my first time, so of course I'm nervous.

examples.japanese: なにせ{忙|いそが}しくて、{連絡|れんらく}する{暇|ひま}もなかった。
examples.english: You see, I was so busy I didn't even have time to get in touch.

examples.japanese: なにせ{相手|あいて}は{世界|せかい}チャンピオンだから、{勝|か}てるとは{思|おも}っていない。
examples.english: After all, the opponent is a world champion, so I don't expect to win.

notes:
A casual conversational variant of なにしろ; both introduce a strong reason or excuse. Placed at the beginning of a sentence or clause, typically followed by から or ので.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- なにせ〜から: after all, because ~
- なにせ〜ので: since, after all, ~
- なにせ〜んだ: the thing is ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- なにしろ: same meaning, slightly more formal
- とにかく: anyway; in any case — less explanatory, often used to redirect a topic
- {何|なん}といっても: above all; most importantly — emphasizes the most outstanding point
